MLB changes Dodgers-Brewers NLCS Game 4 start time due to weather concerns
Major League Baseball adjusted start times for upcoming playoff games involving the Los Angeles Dodgers due to weather concerns elsewhere. The Dodgers trail Milwaukee heading into crucial home games with Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow scheduled as starting pitchers.
Major League Baseball moved up the Los Angeles Dodgers’ Game 4 matchup against the Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday, Oct. 14, changing the start time from 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time to 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time.
The decision followed MLB’s move to reschedule American League Division Series Game 3 between the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays from its original slot at 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time to an earlier start at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time due to forecasted inclement weather in Cleveland.
The Dodgers currently trail the Brewers by two games in the National League Championship Series as they begin a three-game stretch at home. They will attempt to recover ground in Game 3 on Wednesday, which is set for a 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time first pitch.
Blake Snell will take the mound for Los Angeles, aiming to improve on his first postseason start where he walked five batters and pitched just three and two-thirds innings during the team’s only loss of the National League Division Series. Snell previously delivered eight one-hit innings against Milwaukee in last year’s postseason opener.
Snell is set to face left-hander Robert Gasser of Milwaukee, who allowed one run over four innings in his sole appearance this postseason. The Dodgers scored seven runs off Gasser across ten and two-thirds regular season innings and will look for similar success on Wednesday.
Milwaukee has not yet announced its starter for Thursday's fourth game of the series, while Los Angeles plans to send Tyler Glasnow out for his second October start after he held Atlanta Braves hitters to one run through four and two-thirds innings in a previous series-clinching win.
Los Angeles’ offense has struggled so far this series, with hopes that support from home fans can help them mount a comeback as they aim for their franchise’s first three-peat.
